paras.en: Willsey: The principle is to try and get these things as small as possible to disrupt the least amount of tissue as possible, and then to get them really, really close to the individual cells, the neurons themselves that have the information we’re trying to record.
paras.zh: Willsey：原则是尝试让这些东西尽可能小，以尽可能少地破坏组织，然后让它们真正非常接近单个细胞，即拥有我们试图记录信息的神经元本身。

paras.en: Sanders: The goal here is to restore a person’s ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这里的目标是恢复一个人的说话能力。

paras.en: Willsey: So in the ideal situation, the electrodes would sit, you know, right next to those neurons. This type of technology that’s very intuitive, that can record activity from the brain in kind of a high-throughput way, can put the words up at a good speed and a good accuracy, allows them to kind of regain the ability to communicate with others close to how they maybe were before they had the illness. So that truly is very powerful.
paras.zh: 威尔西：所以在理想情况下，电极应该位于那些神经元旁边。这种非常直观的技术，可以以高通量的方式记录大脑的活动，可以以良好的速度和良好的准确性说出单词，使他们能够重新获得与他人沟通的能力，接近他们患病之前的状态。所以这确实是非常强大的。

paras.en: Sanders: You might remember that Casey’s implant, called the BrainGate 2 system, requires ports on his head that are connected to external wires.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：你可能还记得凯西的植入物，称为 BrainGate 2 系统，需要他头上的端口连接到外部电线。

paras.en: Casey: What is annoying about this device is really easy to answer. It is not portable, and it is not implanted only inside my head.
paras.zh: 凯西：这个设备令人烦恼的地方很容易回答。它不是便携式的，也不是只植入我的脑袋里。

paras.en: Sanders: Unlike Casey’s implant, the Paradromics device is fully implantable. That means it’s wireless. This summer, Willsey implanted Paradromic’s device in a volunteer’s brain. The brain belonged to a 68-year-old woman who lives in Michigan. She has primary lateral sclerosis, a disease that has taken away most of her ability to talk. So far, the Paradromics system is up and running, and the volunteer is testing her abilities out.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：与凯西的植入物不同，Paradromics 设备是完全可植入的。这意味着它是无线的。今年夏天，威尔西将 Paradromic 的设备植入一名志愿者的大脑中。大脑属于一位居住在密歇根州的 68 岁女性。她患有原发性侧索硬化症，这种疾病剥夺了她大部分说话的能力。到目前为止，Paradromics 系统已经启动并运行，志愿者正在测试她的能力。

paras.en: Here she is talking with Willsey and other researchers in a video provided by Paradromics. You’ll hear her natural voice, which is hard to understand, and then a digital voice speaking the words her brain implant decoded.
paras.zh: 在 Paradromics 提供的视频中，她正在与威尔西和其他研究人员交谈。你会听到她自然的声音，这很难理解，然后是一个数字声音，说出她的大脑植入解码的单词。

paras.en: [Audio] I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. Yeah, it’s good.
paras.zh: [音频]我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。是的，这很好。

paras.en: Sanders: This volunteer has used the device to talk to her grandkids on the phone. But this is just the very beginning for this research project. There’s so much more to test.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这位志愿者使用该设备与她的孙子们通电话。但这只是这个研究项目的开始。还有很多东西需要测试。

paras.en: Casey is still working on his system, too — particularly, streamlining the process. When Casey uses his brain-computer interface, it decodes speech signals from his brain, then puts words on a screen. Casey then selects a button, using his eye movements or his brain-computer interface, to say these words out loud with a digital voice. Here’s Casey.
paras.zh: 凯西仍在研究他的系统，特别是简化流程。当凯西使用他的脑机接口时，它会解码来自他大脑的语音信号，然后将文字显示在屏幕上。然后，凯西使用他的眼球运动或脑机接口选择一个按钮，用数字语音大声说出这些词。这是凯西。

paras.en: Casey: It is not fast enough to provide enough instant conversation with other people that need to slow down to talk to me.
paras.zh: 凯西：它的速度不够快，无法与其他需要放慢速度与我交谈的人提供足够的即时对话。

paras.en: Sanders: But scientists want to skip this middle part — the words written on a screen. They want instead to go straight to speech, and perhaps make conversations faster. Casey says this goal to go directly from brain signals to a speaking digital voice would be his top priority.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是科学家们想跳过中间部分——屏幕上写的文字。相反，他们希望直接开始讲话，也许可以让对话更快。凯西表示，将大脑信号直接转化为数字语音的目标将是他的首要任务。

paras.en: Casey: That one is the holy grail of what this will become in terms of speech. It will allow you to have a seamless conversation. I am talking about, yes, I will intend to talk, and then it will just translate that automatically into speech, like we do, and you are doing right now.
paras.zh: 凯西：这就是演讲方面的圣杯。它将使您能够进行无缝的对话。我说的是，是的，我打算说话，然后它会自动将其转化为言语，就像我们所做的那样，而你现在正在做的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: In an earlier episode, we talked about attempts to do just this with Casey’s system, to push it to do what they call brain-to-voice. Early attempts were hard to decipher. But it has already improved, by a lot. In the latest tests, this brain-to-voice process produces words that are understandable – reaching about 95 percent accuracy for listeners. Here’s Casey speaking test sentences. It comes from a preprint manuscript posted on the website bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在之前的一集中，我们谈到了尝试用凯西的系统来做到这一点，推动它做他们所谓的“大脑到声音”。早期的尝试很难破译。但它已经改善了很多。在最新的测试中，这种大脑到声音的过程产生了可以理解的单词——对于听众来说准确率达到了 95% 左右。这是凯西口语测试句子。它来自 bioRxiv 网站上发布的预印本手稿。

paras.en: [Audio] The day is not over yet. Please come in with me.
paras.zh: [音频] 这一天还没有结束。请跟我进来。

paras.en: Sanders: Scientists have another thing on their to-do list. And this one goes beyond the words themselves. Here’s Gilja, from Paradromics.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：科学家们的待办事项清单上还有另一件事。这超出了言语本身。这是来自 Paradromics 的 Gilja。

paras.en: Gilja: Let’s say I identify whether a sentence is a statement or a question. Well, now you can pass that information on to speech synthesis, so that you get these two different versions.
paras.zh: Gilja：假设我识别一个句子是陈述还是问题。好吧，现在您可以将该信息传递给语音合成，以便获得这两个不同的版本。

paras.en: Sanders: The same words could be a statement or a question. You see what he means. You see what he means? And that information can be pulled out from a person’s brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：同样的词可以是陈述，也可以是问题。你明白他的意思。你明白他的意思吗？这些信息可以从一个人的大脑活动中提取出来。

paras.en: Gilja: If I’m decoding prosodic information, if I’m decoding speed, when a word is meant to appear, that can also be passed on to modern speech synthesis systems, so that you’re more accurately capturing the prosody that somebody intends. Same thing with loudness, right? So you can see how as that information becomes available from the neural channels, it can be provided to the AI speech synthesis to get closer to the intended voice in the moment that the individual wants to generate.
paras.zh: Gilja：如果我正在解码韵律信息，如果我正在解码速度，当一个单词应该出现时，它也可以传递到现代语音合成系统，这样你就可以更准确地捕捉某人想要的韵律。响度也是一样，对吧？因此，您可以看到，当神经通道提供这些信息时，如何将其提供给人工智能语音合成，以更接近个人想要生成的时刻的预期声音。

paras.en: Sanders: All of these signals can be collected and used to build a more accurate voice — one that says things exactly how a person intends to say them, like a Minnesotan’s ooftah or a slow southern hey y’all. Now, today’s voice clones can add these emotional layers onto words already. Here’s what Jules told me when I asked him about whether his voice clone can do it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所有这些信号都可以被收集并用来构建更准确的声音——一种完全按照一个人想要说的方式说话的声音，就像明尼苏达州的“ooftah”或缓慢的南方“嘿，大家”。现在，今天的语音克隆已经可以将这些情感层添加到单词中。当我问朱尔斯他的声音克隆能否做到这一点时，这是朱尔斯告诉我的。

paras.en: Jules: Oh, there are plenty of things it does that are all the above. But one thing in particular is how it inserts tone and inflections on words. Sometimes my wife will get mad because my response can come off with some sass.
paras.zh: Jules：哦，它做了很多事情，就是上面提到的。但特别的一件事是它如何在单词中插入语气和变化。有时我的妻子会生气，因为我的回答可能有些无礼。

paras.en: Sanders: So there’s loudness, emphasis, pitch — all of these things contribute to what words means. But imagine if a brain implant can pick up these cues directly — no typing required. Here’s Hochberg.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以有响度、强调、音调——所有这些因素都有助于表达单词的含义。但想象一下，如果大脑植入物可以直接接收这些线索——无需打字。这是霍赫伯格。

paras.en: Hochberg: There’s a lot that can be conveyed through the emphasis, through the tone, through even the humor that can sometimes be conveyed by the way that somebody who’s able-bodied may speak a particular sentence. All of those, I think, really can be captured by these implantable brain-computer interfaces by harnessing the rich neural activity that’s available from the brain. We should be able to restore a lot of that.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：通过强调、语气、甚至幽默，可以传达很多东西，有时可以通过身体健全的人说某个特定句子的方式来传达。我认为，所有这些都可以通过利用大脑丰富的神经活动，通过这些植入式脑机接口来捕获。我们应该能够恢复很多。

paras.en: Sanders: Sergey Stavisky is one of the UC Davis researchers working with Casey and Hochberg. He and his colleagues are working on some of these ideas.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西和霍赫伯格一起工作。他和他的同事正在研究其中一些想法。

paras.en: Stavisky: And even now we’re continuing to improve that and actually adding additional layers. So we have one forward-looking project where we can maybe decode the kind of emotional valence of how he’s trying to say it. Is he trying to say something in an angry way or in a surprised way or in a happy-sounding way, to kind of further make it more expressive.
paras.zh: Stavisky：即使现在，我们仍在继续改进这一点，并实际上添加了额外的层。因此，我们有一个前瞻性的项目，我们也许可以解读他试图表达的情感价值。他是否试图以愤怒的方式、惊讶的方式或听起来快乐的方式说某事，以进一步使其更具表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: They’re even trying to decode singing. Well, OK, it’s really more of a hum at this point, he says. But those sorts of tone shifts could, in theory, be deciphered.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们甚至试图解码歌唱。好吧，好吧，现在更多的是嗡嗡声，他说。但从理论上讲，这些语气转变是可以被解读的。

paras.en: Stavisky: We definitely have our work cut out for us on the singing and melody side of things.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：在歌唱和旋律方面，我们确实有很多工作要做。

paras.en: Sanders: All sorts of voice signals could be pulled from brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：各种声音信号都可以从大脑活动中提取。

paras.en: Stavisky: Ultimately, we want people to be in full control of what they’re communicating. This should come from their intent. So, yeah, we are trying to decode all of the aspects of his voice, whether it’s the pitch, the timbre, the loudness, the intonation, which word he’s stressing. All of that, ideally, we would decode from brain activity, including kind of all of that emotional nuance.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：最终，我们希望人们能够完全控制他们所交流的内容。这应该是出于他们的意图。所以，是的，我们正在尝试解码他声音的所有方面，无论是音调、音色、响度、语调，还是他强调的单词。理想情况下，我们可以从大脑活动中解码所有这些，包括所有情感上的细微差别。

paras.en: Sanders: Voice clones can speak with various emotions. You heard my voice clone do just that in earlier episodes. But the difference here is that a person wouldn’t have to type in the instructions. They would come straight from their brain, seamlessly. Other nonverbal signals can be pulled from the brain, too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音克隆可以表达各种情绪。你在之前的剧集中听到我的声音克隆就是这么做的。但这里的区别在于，人们不必输入说明。它们会直接来自他们的大脑，无缝地。其他非语言信号也可以从大脑中提取。

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: In the past five years or so, there have been a lot of advancements in the field of BCIs for restoring individual functions to people with paralysis.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：在过去五年左右的时间里，脑机接口领域在帮助瘫痪患者恢复个人功能方面取得了很多进展。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Samantha Brosler, a bioengineer at the University of California, San Francisco. Some brain-computer interfaces can pick up movements. We haven’t talked much about them, but these implants have their own very successful research history. They’ve allowed people to control a robotic arm, for instance.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是萨曼莎·布罗斯勒，加州大学旧金山分校的生物工程师。一些脑机接口可以接收动作。我们没有过多谈论它们，但这些植入物有自己非常成功的研究历史。例如，他们允许人们控制机械臂。

paras.en: Brosler: Most of these devices so far have been designed to restore one function at a time, whereas in reality, frequently people who are paralyzed are missing both the ability to speak and perform body movements. And so in this study, we asked whether a single brain implant could be used to decode both speech and movement at the same time.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：到目前为止，大多数这些设备的设计目的都是一次恢复一种功能，而实际上，瘫痪的人经常丧失说话和进行身体运动的能力。因此，在这项研究中，我们询问是否可以使用单个大脑植入物同时解码语音和运动。

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out, it could. She and her colleagues were able to decode gestures for communication — things like thumbs up, or a head nodding yes — and words. This combo approach is a more natural way of getting a point across.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明，可以。她和她的同事能够解读交流手势（例如竖起大拇指或点头表示同意）和言语。这种组合方法是一种更自然的表达观点的方式。

paras.en: Brosler: We naturally use gestures alongside our speech. So for example, some gestures can substitute for speech entirely, like nodding yes, shaking your head no, waving, shrugging, giving a thumbs up. But they can also add or change the meaning of what we’re saying. So for example, if you say maybe combined with nod head yes, that has a very different, you know, meaning than if you say maybe and shrug or shake your head no.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们在讲话时自然会使用手势。例如，某些手势可以完全替代言语，例如点头“是”、摇头“不”、挥手、耸肩、竖起大拇指。但他们也可以添加或改变我们所说的话的含义。例如，如果你说“也许”加上点头“是”，这与你说“也许”然后耸耸肩或摇头“不”的含义非常不同。

paras.en: Sanders: My kids know that a slow maybe with a skeptical eyebrow raise is much closer to a no than my fast upbeat maybe with a little head nod. There is so much subtext in our body language.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我的孩子们知道，缓慢地扬起怀疑的眉毛可能比我快速乐观地点头可能更接近于“不”。我们的肢体语言中有很多潜台词。

paras.en: Brosler: So I think of, you know, gestures and body movements as an additional communication channel that can work together with speech to add expressivity to what we’re trying to say.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：所以我认为，手势和身体动作是一种额外的沟通渠道，可以与语音一起工作，为我们想说的话增添表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: In the study, the output was a digital avatar who looked like the person. Success looked like the avatar moving and getting the word right.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在这项研究中，输出的是一个看起来像这个人的数字化身。成功看起来就像化身移动并正确表达了意思。

paras.en: Brosler: And the idea is that we enable the participants to use speech and gestures alone or together. So in theory, someone could say hello while waving.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们的想法是让参与者能够单独或一起使用语音和手势。所以理论上，有人可以一边挥手一边打招呼。

paras.en: Sanders: The researchers started simple, with just a few phrases — hello, bye, good idea, how’s it going, let’s go — and just a few gestures, like a shrug or a point, a fist pump, thumbs up.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：研究人员从简单的开始，只有几句话——你好、再见、好主意、怎么样、走吧——还有几个手势，比如耸肩或点一下、握拳、竖起大拇指。

paras.en: Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: Sanders: The sheer number of different approaches to restoring communication is a sign that this neurotechnology is coming fast. Here’s Willsey.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：恢复沟通的不同方法的数量之多表明这种神经技术正在快速发展。这是威尔西。

paras.en: Willsey: I think it’s good. There’s a lot of players that are entering into the field that have a variety of different ideas where they can run the clinical trials and see how these different devices stack up.
paras.zh: 威尔西：我认为这很好。许多进入该领域的参与者都有各种不同的想法，他们可以进行临床试验，看看这些不同的设备如何叠加。

paras.en: Sanders: There are lots of reasons to be optimistic about the future here, and it’s a future that isn’t even that far off. Here’s David Brandman, one of the researchers at UC Davis who works with Casey. He’s also the neurosurgeon who implanted Casey’s device.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有很多理由对这里的未来感到乐观，而且这个未来并不遥远。这是大卫·布兰德曼（David Brandman），他是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西一起工作。他也是植入凯西设备的神经外科医生。

paras.en: Brandman: I think I’m about five years away from being able to meet a patient with ALS and having the following conversation, and saying, you know, Ms. Smith, I’m sorry you’ve been diagnosed with ALS. I don’t have a cure for you, but I do have a device that I can implant that can help you communicate despite facing a future of paralysis. It’s a device that would be implanted. It’s fully wirelessly. It’s cosmetically invisible, and you’d be able to use it to communicate your needs and have a meaningful conversation with friends and family. So I think that kind of conversation is about five to 10 years away.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我想大约还有五年的时间我就能见到 ALS 患者并进行以下对话，然后说，史密斯女士，我很抱歉您被诊断出患有 ALS。我没有治愈你的方法，但我确实有一种可以植入的设备，可以帮助你在未来面临瘫痪的情况下进行交流。这是一个可以植入的设备。它是完全无线的。它在外观上是隐形的，您可以用它来传达您的需求并与朋友和家人进行有意义的对话。所以我认为这种对话大约需要五到十年的时间。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s a beautiful vision. When you’ve been a reporter as long as I have, you’re skeptical when scientists say something big is just five to 10 years away. But in this case, I see it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是一个美好的愿景。如果你像我一样当了这么久的记者，当科学家说五到十年后就会出现重大事件时，你会持怀疑态度。但在这种情况下，我看到了。

paras.en: It’s easy to get drawn into the technical details here. Different types of implants, the decoding processes, AI-powered voice clones and what they can do and can’t do — what they should do and shouldn’t do. But if you step back and really look, you’ll see that this research is all propelled by a very simple and powerful fact: The human voice is too important to lose.
paras.zh: 这里很容易被技术细节所吸引。不同类型的植入物、解码过程、人工智能驱动的语音克隆以及它们能做什么和不能做什么——它们应该做什么和不应该做什么。但如果你退后一步仔细观察，你会发现这项研究都是由一个非常简单而有力的事实推动的：人的声音太重要了，不能失去。

paras.en: Casey: What does my voice mean to me? It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：我的声音对我来说意味着什么？这意味着很多。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: So now we are here, in this moment, as Jules would say, right here, right now. And right now, the human voice is shifting and changing, expanding in ways that were completely unthinkable even just a few years ago. The future of the human voice and its many replicas is anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以现在我们在这里，此时此刻，正如朱尔斯所说，就在这里，此时此刻。现在，人类的声音正在转变和变化，以几年前完全不可想象的方式扩展。人声及其众多复制品的未来谁也说不准。

paras.en: Sanders: In one of Jules’ comedy sets, the one he did in November of 2024, he wheels out onto the stage as the song “Walking on Sunshine” plays.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在朱尔斯于 2024 年 11 月拍摄的一部喜剧中，他在歌曲《行走在阳光下》中推上舞台。

paras.en: As the crowd settles and finishes their clapping and woo-ing, Jules pauses. You can’t see this, but he wiggles his eyebrows — a lot. The crowd goes crazy every time. He hasn’t said a single word yet. After another pause, he deadpans with his voice clone: “That is all the time I have. My Make-A-Wish covered only a few minutes. Goodnight, everybody.”
paras.zh: 当人群安静下来并结束鼓掌和求爱时，朱尔斯停了下来。你看不到这一点，但他经常摇动眉毛。每次人群都会疯狂。他还没有说一个字。又停顿了一下，他面无表情地用他的声音克隆说：“这就是我所有的时间了。我的愿望只持续了几分钟。大家晚安。”

paras.en: And with that, Jules takes control and he’s off on a tear, ripping through stories of a weatherman who seems too happy about standing out in hurricanes, the exquisite guilt trips lovingly crafted by his Cuban parents, and the indignities of having body parts shaved with his sister right there in the room. Jules has the audience laughing so hard. It’s magnificent.
paras.zh: 就这样，朱尔斯掌控了一切，他泪流满面，讲述了一个天气预报员似乎太高兴在飓风中脱颖而出的故事，他的古巴父母精心设计的精致内疚之旅，以及和他的妹妹一起在房间里剃掉身体部位的侮辱。朱尔斯让观众笑得很厉害。太棒了。

paras.en: MA: And being backstage and then seeing him come out, like roll out in his wheelchair and everybody go nuts because they’re like, what is going on here? Like, this doesn’t make sense. And every time I was like, this is like life. This is love. This is passion. This is like, what else is there? Like, I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here and what I can help him do.
paras.zh: MA：在后台，然后看到他出来，就像坐在轮椅上一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会想，这里发生了什么事？就像，这没有意义。每次我都想，这就像生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。这就像，还有什么？就像，我不知道还有什么比这个人在这里所做的事情以及我可以帮助他做的事情更强大的了。

paras.en: Sanders: I get what MA meant when she said that comedy is something that heals. When his set actually does come to a close, he tells the audience.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我明白马的意思，她说喜剧是一种治愈的东西。当他的演出真正结束时，他告诉观众。

paras.en: [Audio] Now you have to watch me slowly get off this stage. Goodnight, everybody.
paras.zh: [音频]现在你必须看着我慢慢走下这个舞台。大家晚安。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s hilarious. It’s happy. It’s sad. It’s perfect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这很搞笑。很高兴。很伤心。太完美了。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目的帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund, with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Power Grids on 5 Continents Pulse Every 60 Seconds. Scientists Think They Finally Know Why.
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: There are many things about modern life we take for granted – perhaps none more so than the vast electrical grids that power so much of it.
paras.zh: 现代生活中有很多事情我们认为是理所当然的——也许最重要的是为其提供大量电力的庞大电网。

paras.en: But for many years, these grids have been doing something strange.
paras.zh: 但多年来，这些网格一直在做一些奇怪的事情。

paras.en: Every 60 seconds, they pulse – a tiny change in the frequency that subsides only to recur 60 seconds later.
paras.zh: 每 60 秒，它们就会发出一次脉冲——频率的微小变化只会在 60 秒后减弱并再次出现。

paras.en: And it's not just one power grid. Around the world, multiple power grids – physically isolated from each other – have been found doing the same thing.
paras.zh: 而且它不仅仅是一个电网。在世界各地，多个电网（物理上彼此隔离）被发现在做同样的事情。

paras.en: It's precise, and it has persisted, year after year, for more than a decade. This precision suggests that it's not an accident, but it has remained a curiously enduring puzzle.
paras.zh: 它是精确的，并且年复一年地持续了十多年。这种精确性表明这并非偶然，但它仍然是一个令人好奇的持久谜题。

paras.en: Now, scientists think they have found the answer – and it's surprisingly mundane.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们认为他们已经找到了答案——而且答案却出奇地平凡。

paras.en: Every minute, some uninterruptible power supplies – the backup systems used in places like hospitals, data centers, and research facilities – perform routine battery checks, creating small but measurable surges in electricity demand. And it's like clockwork.
paras.zh: 每分钟，一些不间断电源（医院、数据中心和研究设施等场所使用的备用系统）都会执行例行电池检查，从而造成电力需求小幅但可测量的激增。就像发条一样。

paras.en: "Even benign control routines can become systemically relevant when many devices act coherently," writes a team led by physicist Dirk Witthaut of the University of Cologne, Germany, in a paper published in Nature Energy.
paras.zh: 德国科隆大学物理学家 Dirk Witthaut 领导的团队在《自然·能源》杂志上发表的一篇论文中写道：“当许多设备一致行动时，即使是良性的控制程序也会变得系统相关。”

paras.en: "Unintended synchronization can generate recurrent and potentially amplified oscillatory behavior in large-scale cyber-physical energy systems."
paras.zh: “意外的同步可能会在大规模网络物理能源系统中产生反复出现且可能放大的振荡行为。”

paras.en: An electrical grid is always performing a delicate balancing act. At any given moment, the amount of electrical power being produced has to closely match the amount being consumed.
paras.zh: 电网总是在执行微妙的平衡行为。在任何给定时刻，产生的电量必须与消耗的电量紧密匹配。

paras.en: In Britain, there's a name for one of the most glorious examples of the challenge this presents: TV pickup.
paras.zh: 在英国，这种挑战最光荣的例子之一有一个名字：电视拾音。

paras.en: It describes the surge in power demand when large numbers of people collectively turn on their electric kettles to make a cup of tea during commercial breaks in TV programs.
paras.zh: 它描述了当电视节目插播广告时，大量人集体打开电热水壶泡一杯茶时，电力需求激增的情况。

paras.en: It's become less of a problem as grid operators have learned to anticipate it and streaming has gained popularity, but it can still generate massive demand during nationally popular programs such as royal what-have-yous and football matches.
paras.zh: 随着电网运营商已经学会预测这一问题，而且流媒体也越来越受欢迎，这已经不再是一个问题，但在皇家“有什么”和足球比赛等全国流行的节目中，它仍然可以产生大量需求。

paras.en: These fluctuations affect the frequency of the alternating current flowing through the grid – typically 50 or 60 hertz, depending on where in the world you live. When demand exceeds supply, the frequency dips; when supply exceeds demand, it rises.
paras.zh: 这些波动会影响流经电网的交流电的频率——通常为 50 或 60 赫兹，具体取决于您居住在世界的哪个地方。当需求超过供应时，频率就会下降；当供给超过需求时，它就会上升。

paras.en: Usually, these fluctuations are small and irregular, and grid operators work constantly to keep them under control.
paras.zh: 通常，这些波动很小且不规则，电网运营商会不断努力以控制它们。

paras.en: But a fluctuation that repeats with extraordinary precision every 60 seconds? Across electrical grids on five continents that aren't even connected to one another?
paras.zh: 但是每 60 秒就以非凡的精度重复一次的波动呢？横跨五大洲的电网，彼此之间甚至没有连接？

paras.en: Well, that's a whole new kettle of fish.
paras.zh: 好吧，那是一锅全新的鱼。

paras.en: Hints of the phenomenon date back to at least 2014, when researchers in Scandinavia documented unusual minute-scale fluctuations in grid frequency.
paras.zh: 这种现象的迹象至少可以追溯到 2014 年，当时斯堪的纳维亚半岛的研究人员记录了电网频率异常的微小波动。

paras.en: Such oscillations had been linked to hydropower systems, but similar patterns could also be found in electrical grids elsewhere – including continental Europe, Britain, Australia, and the United States.
paras.zh: 这种振荡与水力发电系统有关，但类似的模式也可以在其他地方的电网中发现，包括欧洲大陆、英国、澳大利亚和美国。

paras.en: The fluctuations were small, but remarkably persistent, recurring with extraordinary precision across grids of vastly different sizes and configurations, including systems physically isolated from one another.
paras.zh: 这些波动很小，但非常持久，在大小和配置截然不同的网格（包括物理上彼此隔离的系统）中以非凡的精度重复出现。

paras.en: Whatever was causing the mysterious pulse, hydropower alone couldn't explain it.
paras.zh: 无论是什么引起了神秘的脉冲，仅靠水力发电无法解释它。

paras.en: To figure it out, Witthaut and his colleagues analyzed high-resolution electricity measurements from buildings at the Forschungszentrum Jülich research campus in Germany.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚这一点，Witthaut 和他的同事分析了德国于利希研究中心研究园区建筑物的高分辨率电力测量结果。

paras.en: And this is where the kettle started to heat up – because the 60-second pattern appeared in four buildings, all of which contained uninterruptible power supplies. None of the buildings they measured without these systems showed the same pattern.
paras.zh: 这就是热水壶开始升温的地方——因为 60 秒模式出现在四座建筑物中，所有建筑物都包含不间断电源。他们在没有这些系统的情况下测量的建筑物都没有显示出相同的模式。

paras.en: Following the electrical signals more closely, the researchers detected tiny bursts of current from the batteries at precisely one-minute intervals. They were able to trace the resulting fluctuations through one building's electrical system, all the way to the connection with the public high-voltage grid.
paras.zh: 研究人员更仔细地跟踪电信号，以精确的一分钟间隔检测到电池中的微小电流爆发。他们能够通过一栋建筑物的电力系统追踪由此产生的波动，一直到与公共高压电网的连接。

paras.en: The manufacturer subsequently confirmed the culprit's identity – routine battery self-tests, conducted automatically by the systems' management software.
paras.zh: 制造商随后确认了罪魁祸首的身份——由系统管理软件自动进行的例行电池自检。

paras.en: But why would equipment in different buildings, let alone different countries, be doing this at the same time?
paras.zh: 但为什么不同建筑物（更不用说不同国家）的设备会同时执行此操作？

paras.en: The answer appears to lie in the clocks. Digital devices can synchronize their internal clocks using external time signals, meaning that independently operating systems can end up performing their scheduled tasks together.
paras.zh: 答案似乎就在时钟中。数字设备可以使用外部时间信号同步其内部时钟，这意味着独立的操作系统最终可以一起执行其计划任务。

paras.en: Individually, these small checks are insignificant. But when enough devices act in synchrony, their combined electricity demand can produce a measurable effect across an entire power grid.
paras.zh: 单独来看，这些小额支票微不足道。但是，当足够多的设备同步运行时，它们的综合电力需求可以对整个电网产生可衡量的影响。

paras.en: This explanation will need to be tested in other locations to confirm that the same mechanism is at work, but it's still a rather satisfying solution to a very weird puzzle – and one that could help engineers design more resilient power grids.
paras.zh: 这种解释需要在其他地方进行测试，以确认相同的机制正在发挥作用，但它仍然是解决一个非常奇怪的难题的一个相当令人满意的解决方案，并且可以帮助工程师设计更具弹性的电网。

paras.en: At the moment, the fluctuations pose no immediate threat to grid stability; according to the researchers, they are relatively minor, typically measuring just a few millihertz in amplitude.
paras.zh: 目前，波动不会对电网稳定构成直接威胁；据研究人员称，它们相对较小，通常只能测量几毫赫兹的振幅。

paras.en: But as electricity networks become increasingly dependent on digitally controlled equipment, Witthaut and his colleagues warn that the problem could grow.
paras.zh: 但随着电力网络越来越依赖数字控制设备，威索特和他的同事警告说，这个问题可能会加剧。

paras.en: Battery storage systems, data centers, and internet-connected devices are proliferating, potentially adding more synchronized electrical demands to the grid.
paras.zh: 电池存储系统、数据中心和联网设备正在激增，可能会给电网带来更多同步电力需求。

paras.en: And although the fluctuations are small, they can be amplified by the grid's own dynamics, contributing to wear and tear on equipment such as hydropower turbines.
paras.zh: 尽管波动很小，但电网自身的动态可能会放大波动，从而导致水力发电涡轮机等设备的磨损。

paras.en: Fortunately, the solution may be relatively straightforward, at least for big batteries and backup systems. Rather than having thousands of devices perform the same task at the same moment, manufacturers could introduce small variations into their software schedules, preventing the minutely pile-up.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，该解决方案可能相对简单，至少对于大型电池和备用系统而言是如此。制造商可以在其软件计划中引入微小的变化，从而防止微小的堆积，而不是让数千台设备同时执行相同的任务。

paras.en: "Our results indicate that coherent cyber-physical oscillations can be mitigated directly at their source through improved control design," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们的结果表明，通过改进控制设计，可以直接从源头上减轻相干的网络物理振荡。”

paras.en: Indeed, they have already contacted the manufacturer of one of the systems they identified, and the company issued a software update that relaxed the strict periodicity of its system checks.
paras.zh: 事实上，他们已经联系了他们所识别的系统之一的制造商，该公司发布了软件更新，放宽了系统检查的严格周期。

paras.en: So there we are – mystery solved. Now we can all relax and have a nice cup of tea. Let's just take turns boiling the kettles.
paras.zh: 所以我们就这样——谜团解开了。现在我们都可以放松并喝杯好茶了。我们轮流烧水壶吧。

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Energy.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然能源》杂志上。

articles.title: Scientists Warn of a Growing Tsunami Threat Lurking in Greenland's Fjords
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: A catastrophic landslide in Greenland led to a deadly tsunami, and based on the shape of two other large unstable slopes in the area, scientists are concerned it could happen again.
paras.zh: 格陵兰岛的灾难性山体滑坡引发了致命的海啸，根据该地区另外两个大型不稳定斜坡的形状，科学家担心这种情况可能会再次发生。

paras.en: A Greenland village called Nuugaatsiaq still sits abandoned after the 2017 megatsunami hit the shore with a run-up of about 10 meters (33 feet).
paras.zh: 格陵兰岛的一个名为 Nuugaatsiaq 的村庄在 2017 年特大海啸袭击海岸并上升约 10 米（33 英尺）后仍处于废弃状态。

paras.en: Four inhabitants of Nuugaatsiaq died, and nine more were injured.
paras.zh: 努加特西亚克的四名居民死亡，另有九人受伤。

paras.en: The tsunami originated from a massive landslide in nearby Karrat Fjord. Scientists estimate up to 58 million cubic meters of rock fell from an unstable slope on Ummiammakku Mountain.
paras.zh: 海啸源自附近卡拉特峡湾的大规模山体滑坡。科学家估计，有多达 5800 万立方米的岩石从 Ummiammakku 山不稳定的斜坡上掉落。

paras.en: In a recent paper published in Communications Earth & Environment, geologist Marie Keiding and colleagues from the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland and the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute analyzed two newly identified unstable slopes in the Uummannaq Fjord system.
paras.zh: 在最近发表在《通讯地球与环境》上的一篇论文中，地质学家 Marie Keiding 及其来自丹麦和格陵兰岛地质调查局以及挪威岩土工程研究所的同事分析了乌马纳克峡湾系统中两个新发现的不稳定斜坡。

paras.en: A large slope in Karrat Fjord, just 3 kilometers (1.9 miles) west of the 2017 avalanche, spans 2.65 million square meters above sea level.
paras.zh: 卡拉特峡湾的一个大斜坡位于 2017 年雪崩以西仅 3 公里（1.9 英里）处，海拔 265 万平方米。

paras.en: The researchers estimate there's about 400 million cubic meters of material in that slope, waiting to fall. This makes it one of the world's largest mapped active unstable slopes.
paras.zh: 研究人员估计，该斜坡上约有 4 亿立方米的物质等待掉落。这使其成为世界上最大的已绘制的活动不稳定斜坡之一。

paras.en: Then, there's a smaller "yet more imminent" slope in Kangerluarsuk Fjord. A landslide from this slope would displace around 30 million cubic meters of mountain, according to Keiding and the team's estimates.
paras.zh: 然后，康格鲁阿尔苏克峡湾有一个较小的“但更迫在眉睫”的斜坡。根据凯丁和研究小组的估计，这个斜坡发生的山体滑坡将使大约 3000 万立方米的山体移位。

paras.en: It's this slope that seems to pose the most immediate threat.
paras.zh: 似乎正是这个斜坡构成了最直接的威胁。

paras.en: Prior to 2015, it was barely visible, but since then it has developed very rapidly, perhaps even accelerating.
paras.zh: 2015年之前，它几乎不为人所知，但自那以后，它的发展非常迅速，甚至可能还在加速。

paras.en: "It is likely to fail in whole or in parts within the next few years or decades as a translational rockslide, although the timing of this remains very uncertain," the team writes.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“在未来几年或几十年内，它可能会作为平移岩滑而全部或部分失败，尽管其发生的时间仍然非常不确定。”

paras.en: If this slope falls, it could generate a run-up of 3 to 7 meters at the settlement of Ukkusissat, about 25 kilometers away, which would arrive just 6 minutes after the initial landslide.
paras.zh: 如果该斜坡塌陷，可能会在约 25 公里外的 Ukkusissat 定居点产生 3 至 7 米的上升，该上升将在最初的山体滑坡发生后仅 6 分钟到达。

paras.en: Based on how the 2017 tsunami went down, it's clear that the waves generated by a landslide at Kangerluarsuk Fjord would pose a serious threat to nearby communities.
paras.zh: 根据 2017 年海啸的发生情况，康厄鲁阿尔苏克峡湾山体滑坡产生的波浪显然会对附近社区构成严重威胁。

paras.en: But if the entire Karrat Fjord unstable slope were to fail, tsunamis as tall as telephone poles could ricochet across the entire Uummannaq Fjord system.
paras.zh: 但如果整个卡拉特峡湾不稳定的斜坡崩塌，电线杆那么高的海啸可能会席卷整个乌马纳克峡湾系统。

paras.en: "While the deep-seated deformation of the Karrat unstable slope appears to be long-term and relatively slow, a collapse of the entire unstable slope cannot be excluded," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“虽然卡拉特不稳定斜坡的深层变形似乎是长期且相对缓慢的，但不能排除整个不稳定斜坡的崩塌。”

paras.en: "Such a failure could generate a tsunami with run-up exceeding 10 meters more than 100 kilometers away, demonstrating the far-reaching impact of such an event."
paras.zh: “这样的故障可能会在100多公里外引发超过10米的海啸，这表明了此类事件的深远影响。”

paras.en: Landslides are a normal process in fjords, but scientists think climate change may be playing a part in the growing risk of such catastrophic landslide activity in Arctic areas by melting the permafrost.
paras.zh: 山体滑坡是峡湾的正常过程，但科学家认为，气候变化可能通过永久冻土融化，导致北极地区发生此类灾难性山体滑坡活动的风险不断增加。

paras.en: "These slopes and the tsunamis they may cause illustrate an emerging
paras.zh: “这些斜坡及其可能引起的海啸说明了一种正在出现的情况

paras.en: hazard in Arctic and high-mountain areas, where progressive permafrost
paras.zh: 北极和高山地区的危险，那里的永久冻土不断增加

paras.en: degradation associated with global warming will increase the frequency and
paras.zh: 与全球变暖相关的退化将增加频率和

paras.en: magnitude of such events," Keiding and team conclude.
paras.zh: 此类事件的严重性，”Keiding 和团队总结道。

paras.en: The research has been published in Communications Earth & Environment.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《通讯地球与环境》杂志上。

articles.title: Science Has Finally Shown That Your Cat Meows to Demand That You Fix Their World
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: We hate to be the ones to break it to you, but your cat may have some complaints about the service you're delivering.
paras.zh: 我们不想向您透露这一点，但您的猫可能会对您提供的服务有一些抱怨。

paras.en: Those yowls and yells, and howls and mewls, could be your cat's way, not just of voicing dissatisfaction with the world, but deliberately trying to get your attention so you can fix it.
paras.zh: 那些嚎叫、叫喊、嚎叫和喵喵声可能是你的猫的方式，不仅仅是表达对世界的不满，而是故意试图引起你的注意，以便你可以解决它。

paras.en: It's OK if you've missed it. Humans are, after all, notoriously bad at understanding what our feline friends are trying to say.
paras.zh: 如果您错过了也没关系。毕竟，人类在理解我们的猫科动物朋友想说的话方面是出了名的糟糕。

paras.en: But a new study has shown that you, officially, may be the fix-it department in your cat's life.
paras.zh: 但一项新的研究表明，正式来说，你可能是你的猫生活中的修复部门。

paras.en: Animal behaviorists at the University of São Paulo in Brazil introduced a problem into the lives of 38 pet cats – and observed what happened when their humans were or were not around to fix it.
paras.zh: 巴西圣保罗大学的动物行为学家将一个问题引入 38 只宠物猫的生活中，并观察当人类在场或不在场时会发生什么情况来解决这个问题。

paras.en: And the cats were four times more shouty when their favorite lackeys were around.
paras.zh: 当它们最喜欢的走狗在附近时，猫的叫喊声会增加四倍。

paras.en: "These results are consistent with meowing playing a communicative role in cat-human interactions," the researchers write in a paper published in Animal Behaviour.
paras.zh: 研究人员在《动物行为》杂志上发表的一篇论文中写道：“这些结果与喵喵在猫与人的互动中发挥的交流作用是一致的。”

paras.en: Cats have a diverse and often very subtle repertoire of communication skills at their disposal, but one in particular seems like it might have been honed for dealing with rather less subtle human butlers – the meow.
paras.zh: 猫拥有多种且通常非常微妙的沟通技巧，但其中一种似乎是为了与不那么微妙的人类管家打交道而磨练出来的——喵喵声。

paras.en: We've known for decades that cats meow frequently and sometimes loudly in the presence of humans, but relatively rarely in the presence of their own kind.
paras.zh: 几十年来，我们都知道猫在人类面前经常喵喵叫，有时甚至大声喵叫，但在同类面前相对很少。

paras.en: In addition, feral cats meow far less frequently than their pet counterparts, suggesting that something about the behavior has to do with proximity to humans.
paras.zh: 此外，野猫喵喵叫的频率远低于宠物猫，这表明这种行为与与人类的亲近有关。

paras.en: Scientists have suspected that something has to do with getting humans to do things, even down to different types of meows for food, for pets, or for access through closed doors.
paras.zh: 科学家们怀疑，这与让人类做事有关，甚至是为了食物、宠物或关上门而发出不同类型的喵叫。

paras.en: But there's a difference between yowling out of sheer annoyance and shouting at Jeeves to come and make the thing happen.
paras.zh: 但纯粹出于恼怒而嚎叫和对吉夫斯大喊让事情发生是有区别的。

paras.en: And this is where Naila Fukimoto of the University of São Paulo and her colleagues come in with their snacks.
paras.zh: 这就是圣保罗大学的 Naila Fukimoto 和她的同事带着零食进来的地方。

paras.en: The researchers recruited 38 pet cats whose humans reported quite a lot of meowing if food was involved.
paras.zh: 研究人员招募了 38 只宠物猫，人类报告称，如果涉及到食物，它们就会发出大量的喵叫声。

paras.en: Each cat was then given a life-or-death problem they could not solve alone: a favorite food treat in a small plastic box with holes in it. The cat could smell the treat. They knew it was in there. But they could not get it with their own resources.
paras.zh: 然后，每只猫都会面临一个它们无法单独解决的生死攸关的问题：在一个有孔的小塑料盒里放一份最喜欢的食物。猫能闻到零食的味道。他们知道它就在那里。但他们无法凭借自己的资源获得它。

paras.en: They needed a tool that only a human could provide: opposable thumbs.
paras.zh: 他们需要一种只有人类才能提供的工具：对生拇指。

paras.en: The researchers then observed what happened over one minute under two different conditions: with a human present and paying attention, or with no human in the room.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员观察了两种不同条件下一分钟内发生的情况：有人在场并集中注意力，或者房间里没有人。

paras.en: If there was a human with whom to register a complaint, those cats got noisy.
paras.zh: 如果有人可以投诉，那些猫就会吵闹。

paras.en: The researchers recorded a total of 86 meows when a human was present, compared to a measly 20 meows if the cat was all alone. A statistical analysis revealed that the odds of meowing were more than 16 times higher when a human was in the room.
paras.zh: 当有人在场时，研究人员总共记录了 86 次喵叫声，相比之下，当猫独自一人时，只记录了区区 20 次喵叫声。统计分析显示，当房间里有人时，喵喵叫的几率要高出 16 倍以上。

paras.en: And they were, indeed, yowling about their problems.
paras.zh: 事实上，他们正在为自己的问题大喊大叫。

paras.en: The researchers also recorded what the cats did when they were meowing.
paras.zh: 研究人员还记录了猫喵喵叫时的行为。

paras.en: They often directed their limpid gazes toward the human, sometimes alternating between their would-be savior and the snack box – what certainly looked like a plea to do something about the current unacceptable situation.
paras.zh: 它们经常将清澈的目光投向人类，有时在潜在的救世主和零食盒之间交替——这看起来确实像是在恳求对当前不可接受的情况采取一些行动。

paras.en: In addition, if the human was not present, the cat spent more time standing still and looking at the door.
paras.zh: 此外，如果人类不在场，猫就会花更多的时间站着不动，看着门口。

paras.en: This suggests that the cats were not just yelling about the unfair state of the world, but adjusting their behavior depending on who might be available to fix it.
paras.zh: 这表明猫不仅仅是大喊大叫世界的不公平状况，而是根据谁可以解决问题来调整自己的行为。

paras.en: That doesn't necessarily mean the cats consciously understood that their humans could solve the problem, or that every meow was a deliberate request. But it does suggest that meowing is more than just an involuntary expression of feline feelings.
paras.zh: 这并不一定意味着猫有意识地理解它们的人类可以解决问题，或者每一次喵叫都是有意的请求。但这确实表明，喵喵不仅仅是猫科动物情感的无意识表达。

paras.en: "The recipient-directed nature of the majority of meows recorded in our study indicates that cats were not simply vocalizing into the environment but targeting a specific audience, consistent with recipient-specific signaling," the researchers write in their paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在论文中写道：“我们的研究中记录的大多数喵喵声的面向接受者的性质表明，猫不仅仅是向环境发声，而是针对特定的受众，这与接受者特定的信号一致。”

paras.en: There are some caveats. The study was relatively small, and the researchers deliberately recruited cats already known to be vocal about food. The results may not apply quite so neatly to cats who prefer to suffer their indignities in silence.
paras.zh: 有一些注意事项。这项研究规模相对较小，研究人员特意招募了已知会对食物发声的猫。对于那些喜欢默默忍受侮辱的猫来说，这个结果可能不太适用。

paras.en: Future studies may also involve profiling the actual meows and comparing them to meows in other situations, to see if the cats use different vocalizations for different requests.
paras.zh: 未来的研究还可能涉及对实际的喵叫进行分析，并将其与其他情况下的喵叫进行比较，看看猫是否会针对不同的请求使用不同的发声。

paras.en: But for anyone who has lived with one of these fuzzy little divas, the results may not come as a surprise.
paras.zh: 但对于任何与这些毛茸茸的小女主角一起生活过的人来说，结果可能并不令人意外。

paras.en: After all, we all know this street only goes one way. And it's totally worth it.
paras.zh: 毕竟，我们都知道这条街只有一个方向。这是完全值得的。

paras.en: The research has been published in Animal Behaviour.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《动物行为》杂志上。

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028

paras.en: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
paras.zh: NASA 公布了 2028 年让宇航员重返月球的大胆新计划

paras.en: - NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
paras.zh: - NASA 公布了一项加速计划，计划于 2028 年将宇航员送上月球，SpaceX 和 Blue Origin 正在开发竞争性的月球着陆器，并计划于 2027 年进行一项关键的轨道测试。更快的火箭准备工作、新型轻型宇航服和重新设计的任务可能有助于为永久登月和未来人类探索火星铺平道路。

paras.en: NASA has revealed new details about its accelerated effort to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028. The updated strategy includes testing two competing lunar landers, streamlining rocket preparations, and introducing a lighter spacesuit to help make the first moonwalks possible sooner.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 透露了有关加速在 2028 年让美国宇航员重返月球的新细节。更新后的战略包括测试两个相互竞争的月球着陆器、简化火箭准备工作，以及引入更轻的宇航服，以帮助更快地实现首次月球漫步。

paras.en: During an October 23 briefing, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders outlined the next steps for the Artemis program. The revised approach centers on two major missions: Artemis III, a test flight scheduled for 2027, and Artemis IV, which is intended to land astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028.
paras.zh: 在 10 月 23 日的新闻发布会上，美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼和其他机构领导人概述了阿耳忒弥斯计划的后续步骤。修订后的方法集中于两项主要任务：阿耳忒弥斯 III（计划于 2027 年进行试飞）和阿耳忒弥斯 IV（计划于 2028 年将宇航员登陆月球表面）。

paras.en: The announcement builds on priorities introduced earlier this year through NASA's Ignition initiative. Agency officials also highlighted recent progress in spacecraft development, mission preparations, and partnerships with private aerospace companies. These efforts are intended to reduce technical risks, accelerate the schedule, and establish the foundation for a lasting American presence on the Moon.
paras.zh: 该公告建立在今年早些时候通过 NASA 的 Ignition 计划推出的优先事项的基础上。该机构官员还强调了航天器开发、任务准备以及与私营航空航天公司合作方面的最新进展。这些努力旨在降低技术风险，加快进度，并为美国在月球上的持久存在奠定基础。

paras.en: "This is a very energized NASA, and these updates are only a small part of that story. We are bringing extreme focus to the mission to ensure delivery of world-changing outcomes as quickly, safely, affordably, and successfully as possible," said Isaacman. "NASA is driving outcomes to make Moon missions a reality, and we're not waiting for others to bring their plans to us -- the campaign must move with urgency as strategic competitors pursue a permanent presence beyond Earth."
paras.zh: 艾萨克曼说：“这是一个充满活力的美国宇航局，这些更新只是这个故事的一小部分。我们将高度关注这项任务，以确保尽可能快速、安全、经济和成功地交付改变世界的成果。” “美国宇航局正在推动成果，使月球任务成为现实，我们不会等待其他人向我们提出他们的计划 - 随着战略竞争对手寻求在地球之外永久存在，这项活动必须紧急开展。”

paras.en: Artemis III Will Test Two Lunar Landers in Earth Orbit
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯三号将在地球轨道上测试两个月球着陆器

paras.en: Before attempting another crewed Moon landing, NASA plans to conduct a major rehearsal in Earth orbit. The Artemis III mission will bring together NASA's Orion spacecraft and experimental lunar landers developed by SpaceX and Blue Origin.
paras.zh: 在尝试另一次载人登月之前，美国宇航局计划在地球轨道上进行一次大型演习。 Artemis III 任务将汇集 NASA 的猎户座飞船以及 SpaceX 和 Blue Origin 开发的实验性月球着陆器。

paras.en: Four astronauts will travel aboard Orion, launching on NASA's powerful SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During the planned 14-day mission, the crew will practice rendezvous and docking procedures with both companies' lander test vehicles. Rendezvous involves guiding two spacecraft to meet in orbit, while docking allows them to connect so astronauts can move between vehicles.
paras.zh: 四名宇航员将搭乘猎户座飞船，乘坐 NASA 强大的 SLS（太空发射系统）火箭发射升空。在计划的 14 天任务中，机组人员将与两家公司的着陆器测试飞行器练习交会对接程序。交会涉及引导两个航天器在轨道上相遇，而对接则允许它们连接，以便宇航员可以在飞行器之间移动。

paras.en: These demonstrations are designed to verify important spacecraft capabilities before Artemis IV attempts to carry astronauts to the Moon's surface.
paras.zh: 这些演示旨在在阿耳忒弥斯四号尝试将宇航员运送到月球表面之前验证重要的航天器功能。

paras.en: The tests will take place in a carefully planned sequence. Blue Origin will first launch a test version of its Blue Moon lander into Earth orbit. NASA will then send Orion and its four astronauts into space aboard the SLS rocket, where Orion will rendezvous and dock with the Blue Moon vehicle.
paras.zh: 测试将按仔细计划的顺序进行。蓝色起源将首先将其蓝月着陆器的测试版本发射到地球轨道。随后，美国宇航局将乘坐 SLS 火箭将猎户座及其四名宇航员送入太空，猎户座将在那里与蓝月飞行器交会对接。

paras.en: Next, SpaceX will launch a test version of its Version 3 Starship lunar lander. Orion will separate from Blue Moon and perform another docking maneuver, this time with Starship. By testing both systems during a single crewed mission, NASA aims to gather essential operational experience while reducing uncertainties before the 2028 landing attempt.
paras.zh: 接下来，SpaceX 将发射其 Version 3 Starship 月球着陆器的测试版本。猎户座将与蓝月亮分离并进行另一次对接机动，这次是与星舰。通过在一次载人任务中测试这两个系统，NASA 的目标是在 2028 年着陆尝试之前收集必要的操作经验，同时减少不确定性。

paras.en: NASA Cuts Rocket Preparation Times and Costs
paras.zh: 美国宇航局削减火箭准备时间和成本

paras.en: The new mission details follow other recent Artemis progress reports. According to NASA, the hardware needed for Artemis III remains on schedule, and improvements in processing have reduced preparation timelines by approximately 50%.
paras.zh: 新任务的详细信息遵循最近的其他阿尔忒弥斯进度报告。据 NASA 称，Artemis III 所需的硬件仍然按计划进行，处理过程的改进将准备时间缩短了约 50%。

paras.en: The agency also reported a significant engineering achievement involving a critical rocket fuel-line component. Rather than relying on an outside supplier, NASA engineers redesigned, manufactured, and tested the component themselves in just five months. The work cost roughly one-tenth of an earlier estimate from an external vendor.
paras.zh: 该机构还报告了一项涉及关键火箭燃料管线部件的重大工程成就。 NASA 工程师没有依赖外部供应商，而是在短短五个月内自行重新设计、制造和测试了该组件。工作成本大约是外部供应商先前估计的十分之一。

paras.en: "NASA should be expected to do this kind of work, and we have some of the best technical knowledge in the world on rocket hardware and operations to do it," said Jeremy Parsons, the agency's Artemis program manager. "It's an example of how we are rebuilding our core competencies and developing centers of excellence in technical functions instead of continuing to outsource expertise."
paras.zh: “NASA 应该能够开展此类工作，我们在火箭硬件和操作方面拥有世界上最好的技术知识来完成这项工作，”该机构的阿耳忒弥斯项目经理杰里米·帕森斯 (Jeremy Parsons) 说。 “这是我们如何重建核心能力和发展技术职能卓越中心而不是继续外包专业知识的一个例子。”

paras.en: The improvements reflect NASA's broader effort to strengthen its internal engineering capabilities, shorten development schedules, and reduce the cost of preparing missions for launch.
paras.zh: 这些改进反映了美国宇航局在加强其内部工程能力、缩短开发时间表和降低发射任务准备成本方面所做的更广泛的努力。

paras.en: SpaceX and Blue Origin Offer Different Paths to the Moon
paras.zh: SpaceX 和蓝色起源提供不同的登月路径

paras.en: For Artemis IV in 2028, NASA intends to launch astronauts aboard Orion using the SLS rocket from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Once in space, the crew will rely on a lunar landing system developed by either SpaceX or Blue Origin to reach the Moon's surface.
paras.zh: 对于 2028 年的阿尔忒弥斯 IV，NASA 打算使用佛罗里达州肯尼迪航天中心的 SLS 火箭将宇航员送上猎户座。一旦进入太空，宇航员将依靠 SpaceX 或 Blue Origin 开发的月球着陆系统到达月球表面。

paras.en: Both companies have revised their original mission designs to make operations simpler, more efficient, and more adaptable. Although they share the same objective, their approaches to transporting astronauts to the lunar surface differ considerably.
paras.zh: 两家公司都修改了最初的任务设计，使操作更简单、更高效、适应性更强。尽管他们有着相同的目标，但他们将宇航员运送到月球表面的方法却有很大不同。

paras.en: SpaceX plans to use its Starship spacecraft, which will take on additional propellant while orbiting Earth. After refueling, Starship will meet Orion and carry the spacecraft toward the Moon. Refueling in orbit is an important part of SpaceX's strategy because it allows the vehicle to receive the propellant needed for its journey after leaving the launchpad.
paras.zh: SpaceX 计划使用其 Starship 航天器，该航天器将在绕地球运行时携带额外的推进剂。加油后，星舰将与猎户座相遇，并载着飞船前往月球。在轨加油是 SpaceX 战略的重要组成部分，因为它允许飞行器在离开发射台后接收旅程所需的推进剂。

paras.en: Blue Origin is developing a different approach using its Blue Moon Mark 2 lander. Its plan calls for additional propulsion stages in Earth orbit to send the lander toward the Moon. The lander will then meet Orion in a relatively low lunar orbit before carrying astronauts down to the surface.
paras.zh: 蓝色起源正在利用其 Blue Moon Mark 2 着陆器开发一种不同的方法。它的计划要求在地球轨道上增加额外的推进级，以将着陆器送向月球。然后，着陆器将在相对较低的月球轨道上与猎户座相遇，然后将宇航员带到月球表面。

paras.en: Both companies are working toward having their systems ready to support a crewed Moon landing in 2028. Maintaining two potential landing systems gives NASA greater flexibility as development and testing continue.
paras.zh: 两家公司都在努力让自己的系统为 2028 年载人登月做好准备。随着开发和测试的继续，维护两个潜在的着陆系统为 NASA 提供了更大的灵活性。

paras.en: NASA Explores New Rocket Options for Artemis IV
paras.zh: NASA 探索阿耳忒弥斯 IV 的新火箭选择

paras.en: NASA is also considering two possible upper stages for the SLS rocket used on Artemis IV. An upper stage is the portion of a rocket that provides additional propulsion after the earlier stages have completed their work, helping send a spacecraft toward its destination.
paras.zh: NASA 还在考虑阿耳忒弥斯 IV 上使用的 SLS 火箭的两个可能的上级。上级是火箭的一部分，在前几级完成工作后提供额外的推进力，帮助将航天器送向目的地。

paras.en: One option is the interim cryogenic propulsion stage already used by SLS. The other is an extended version of United Launch Alliance's Centaur V upper stage, which would hold additional propellant.
paras.zh: 一种选择是 SLS 已经使用的临时低温推进级。另一种是联合发射联盟半人马座 V 上级的扩展版本，可容纳额外的推进剂。

paras.en: By developing both possibilities, NASA hopes to preserve flexibility in its launch plans and avoid becoming dependent on a single technical solution. Having alternatives could help the agency respond to engineering challenges without jeopardizing the broader Moon landing schedule.
paras.zh: 通过开发这两种可能性，美国宇航局希望保持其发射计划的灵活性，并避免依赖单一的技术解决方案。拥有替代方案可以帮助该机构应对工程挑战，而不会危及更广泛的登月计划。

paras.en: A New Lightweight Spacesuit Could Speed Up Moonwalks
paras.zh: 新型轻型宇航服可以加快月球行走速度

paras.en: Another important change involves the spacesuits astronauts will wear while exploring the lunar surface.
paras.zh: 另一个重要的变化涉及宇航员在探索月球表面时所穿的宇航服。

paras.en: NASA is working with Axiom Space on a second, lighter design known as the "Sortie suit." The new suit is intended specifically for the first Moon surface excursions and weighs approximately half as much as Axiom's larger primary spacesuit.
paras.zh: NASA 正在与 Axiom Space 合作开发第二种更轻的设计，称为“Sortie 套装”。这款新宇航服专为首次月球表面游览而设计，重量约为 Axiom 较大的主宇航服的一半。

paras.en: The lighter design could simplify preparations for the earliest landing missions and help astronauts begin exploring the lunar surface sooner.
paras.zh: 更轻的设计可以简化最早着陆任务的准备工作，并帮助宇航员更快地开始探索月球表面。

paras.en: However, the Sortie suit is not intended to replace the primary design. Axiom's more capable suit will remain part of NASA's plans for future missions that require longer periods outside the spacecraft and more demanding surface activities.
paras.zh: 然而，突击服并不打算取代主要设计。 Axiom 功能更强大的宇航服仍将是 NASA 未来任务计划的一部分，这些任务需要在航天器外停留更长的时间并进行更苛刻的表面活动。

paras.en: Building a Permanent Human Presence on the Moon
paras.zh: 在月球上建立人类永久存在

paras.en: NASA's ambitions extend well beyond returning astronauts to the lunar surface for a single mission.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局的野心远远超出了将宇航员送回月球表面执行单一任务。

paras.en: As the Artemis program advances, the agency intends to send crews on increasingly challenging expeditions near the Moon's South Pole. This region is an important focus of future lunar exploration, and the missions are designed to expand how much of the Moon humans can investigate directly.
paras.zh: 随着阿耳忒弥斯计划的进展，该机构打算派遣宇航员前往月球南极附近进行越来越具有挑战性的探险。该区域是未来月球探索的重要焦点，这些任务旨在扩大人类可以直接探索月球的范围。

paras.en: NASA describes the effort as part of a new Golden Age of innovation and exploration. The agency expects its lunar missions to support scientific discoveries, generate economic benefits, and encourage the development of technologies needed for more ambitious space exploration.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局将这一努力描述为创新和探索的新黄金时代的一部分。该机构期望其月球任务能够支持科学发现，产生经济效益，并鼓励开发更雄心勃勃的太空探索所需的技术。

paras.en: Ultimately, the goal is to establish an enduring human presence on the Moon rather than repeat the brief visits of earlier lunar expeditions. The experience gained from operating spacecraft, supporting astronauts, and carrying out increasingly complex missions on the lunar surface will also help NASA prepare for another historic objective: sending the first astronauts to Mars.
paras.zh: 最终的目标是在月球上建立持久的人类存在，而不是重复早期月球探险的短暂访问。从操作航天器、支持宇航员以及在月球表面执行日益复杂的任务中获得的经验也将帮助美国宇航局为另一个历史性目标做好准备：将第一批宇航员送往火星。

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space

paras.en: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
paras.zh: 加州理工学院机器人通过在太空中建造结构创造历史

paras.en: - For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
paras.zh: - 机器人首次在太空中自主建造部分结构，展示了可能从根本上改变太空探索的突破。有一天，这项技术可以让科学家们在轨道上建造巨大的望远镜、通信天线和太阳能发电站，远远超出当今火箭的尺寸限制。

paras.en: For the first time, a robot has successfully assembled part of a structure in space without astronauts, demonstrating a technology that could dramatically change how large spacecraft and scientific instruments are built.
paras.zh: 机器人首次在没有宇航员的情况下成功地在太空中组装了部分结构，展示了一项可以极大改变大型航天器和科学仪器建造方式的技术。

paras.en: The robotic system was developed by researchers at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) with funding from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA). It is part of DARPA's Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D) program, an initiative exploring ways to manufacture and assemble enormous structures directly in space.
paras.zh: 该机器人系统是由加州理工学院 (Caltech) 的研究人员在国防高级研究计划局 (DARPA) 的资助下开发的。它是 DARPA 新型轨道和月球制造、材料和质量效率设计 (NOM4D) 计划的一部分，该计划探索直接在太空中制造和组装巨大结构的方法。

paras.en: Rather than relying on astronauts to connect individual pieces, the robot uses an automated arm to retrieve structural tubes and connecting joints from nearby storage dispensers. It then joins the components into repeating sections, called bays, that form a larger supporting framework known as a truss.
paras.zh: 该机器人不是依靠宇航员连接各个部件，而是使用自动手臂从附近的存储分配器中检索结构管和连接接头。然后，它将组件连接成重复的部分（称为间隔），形成一个更大的支撑框架（称为桁架）。

paras.en: "This is the first time that a structure has been autonomously constructed in space," says Sergio Pellegrino, the Joyce and Krent Kresa Professor of Aerospace and Civil Engineering, the Lynn Booth and Kent Kresa Department of Aerospace Leadership Chair, the executive officer for aerospace, and a senior research scientist at JPL, which Caltech manages for NASA.
paras.zh: “这是第一次在太空中自主建造结构，”航空航天与土木工程系乔伊斯和克伦特·克雷萨教授、林恩·布斯和肯特·克雷萨航空航天部领导主席、航空航天执行官、喷气推进实验室（加州理工学院为 NASA 管理）的高级研究科学家塞尔吉奥·佩莱格里诺 (Sergio Pellegrino) 说。

paras.en: A Historic Step Toward Building Giant Structures in Space
paras.zh: 迈向建造太空巨型结构的历史性一步

paras.en: Pellegrino leads Caltech's Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA) demonstration. The robotic system has spent six months in orbit attempting to construct a reflector antenna measuring 1.4 meters across. Its design combines composite fiber tubes, aluminum connectors, and a lightweight reflective surface made from Kapton, a durable polymer film commonly used in spacecraft.
paras.zh: Pellegrino 领导了加州理工学院的自主太空张紧反射器组件 (ASTRA) 演示。该机器人系统在轨道上花了六个月的时间试图建造一个直径为 1.4 米的反射器天线。其设计结合了复合纤维管、铝连接器和由 Kapton（一种航天器中常用的耐用聚合物薄膜）制成的轻质反射表面。

paras.en: DARPA compares the assembly process to building with sophisticated versions of K'Nex or Tinkertoy construction toys. However, making a robot perform those same tasks reliably in the harsh environment of space presents a far greater engineering challenge.
paras.zh: DARPA 将组装过程与使用复杂版本的 K'Nex 或 Tinkertoy 建筑玩具进行建造进行了比较。然而，让机器人在恶劣的太空环境中可靠地执行相同的任务提出了更大的工程挑战。

paras.en: The team encountered technical difficulties and scheduling constraints that prevented it from finishing the entire antenna. Nevertheless, the robot successfully assembled an initial section, providing evidence that this construction method can work in orbit. Researchers believe the same basic approach could eventually support much larger frameworks carrying enormous reflective surfaces.
paras.zh: 该团队遇到了技术困难和进度限制，无法完成整个天线。尽管如此，机器人还是成功地组装了初始部分，证明这种施工方法可以在轨道上发挥作用。研究人员相信，同样的基本方法最终可以支持承载巨大反射表面的更大框架。

paras.en: The orbital experiment represents the third stage of DARPA's research program. During the first two stages, Caltech researchers developed the construction concept, worked out the engineering design, and verified its operation in laboratory experiments on Earth. The team then had less than 12 months to manufacture, test, and deliver the space hardware to Momentus Inc., the company hosting the payload.
paras.zh: 轨道实验代表了 DARPA 研究计划的第三阶段。在前两个阶段，加州理工学院的研究人员开发了建造概念，制定了工程设计，并在地球上的实验室实验中验证了其运行情况。随后，该团队用不到 12 个月的时间来制造、测试太空硬件，并将其交付给托管有效载荷的 Momentus Inc. 公司。

paras.en: "Developing a payload of this complexity on such a short timeline was an enormous undertaking for our small team," says Pellegrino, who is also co-director of the Space Solar Power Project, which aims to harvest solar power in space and wirelessly transmit it to Earth's surface. "As we wrap up the mission, we are finally able to start thinking about the new avenues of research opened by this demonstration."
paras.zh: “在如此短的时间内开发如此复杂的有效载荷对于我们的小团队来说是一项艰巨的任务，”佩莱格里诺说，他也是太空太阳能发电项目的联合主任，该项目的目标是在太空收集太阳能并将其无线传输到地球表面。 “当我们完成任务时，我们终于能够开始思考这次演示所开辟的新研究途径。”

paras.en: Why Scientists Want to Build Enormous Structures in Orbit
paras.zh: 为什么科学家想要在轨道上建造巨大的结构

paras.en: The ability to assemble large structures directly in space could transform astronomy, communications, and space based energy systems.
paras.zh: 直接在太空中组装大型结构的能力可以改变天文学、通信和基于太空的能源系统。

paras.en: For example, future telescopes could use enormous reflective surfaces to collect more light and observe extremely distant objects. Similar structures could also support powerful radio antennas, allowing scientists and engineers to build communications systems much larger than those that can currently be launched.
paras.zh: 例如，未来的望远镜可以使用巨大的反射表面来收集更多的光并观察极远的物体。类似的结构还可以支持强大的无线电天线，使科学家和工程师能够构建比目前可以发射的系统大得多的通信系统。

paras.en: One of the greatest obstacles is the limited room available inside a rocket's fairing, the protective enclosure that surrounds its payload during launch. No matter how ambitious a spacecraft design might be, its components must somehow fit inside that confined space.
paras.zh: 最大的障碍之一是火箭整流罩内的可用空间有限，整流罩是发射期间围绕其有效载荷的保护外壳。无论航天器的设计多么雄心勃勃，其组件都必须以某种方式安装在这个有限的空间内。

paras.en: Traditionally, engineers have addressed this problem in two ways. They either fold large structures into compact packages that can unfold after reaching orbit, or they launch separate components and have astronauts assemble them in space. Both approaches impose practical limits on the size and complexity of the finished structure.
paras.zh: 传统上，工程师通过两种方式解决这个问题。它们要么将大型结构折叠成紧凑的包裹，以便在到达轨道后展开，要么发射单独的部件并让宇航员在太空中组装它们。这两种方法都对最终结构的尺寸和复杂性施加了实际限制。

paras.en: Robotic construction offers a third possibility. Instead of fitting an enormous telescope or antenna inside a rocket, engineers could transport its materials into orbit and assemble the complete system there.
paras.zh: 机器人建造提供了第三种可能性。工程师无需在火箭内安装巨大的望远镜或天线，而是可以将其材料运送到轨道并在那里组装完整的系统。

paras.en: DARPA's Plan for Kilometer-Scale Space Structures
paras.zh: DARPA 公里级空间结构计划

paras.en: DARPA established NOM4D in 2022 to investigate technologies that could eventually "ferry raw materials from Earth for in-orbit manufacturing," according to the program's website.
paras.zh: 据该项目网站称，DARPA 于 2022 年建立了 NOM4D，以研究最终能够“从地球运送原材料用于在轨制造”的技术。

paras.en: Caltech's ASTRA experiment is one of only two projects selected to advance to the program's third phase, which involves demonstrating construction technologies in orbit.
paras.zh: 加州理工学院的 ASTRA 实验是仅有的两个被选中进入该计划第三阶段的项目之一，该阶段涉及在轨道上展示施工技术。

paras.en: The other project, led by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, will use a module attached to the International Space Station to investigate a technique for hardening carbon tubes in space. This could provide another way to manufacture structural components without having to complete every step on Earth.
paras.zh: 另一个项目由伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校领导，将使用连接到国际空间站的模块来研究在太空中硬化碳管的技术。这可以提供另一种制造结构部件的方法，而无需在地球上完成每一步。

paras.en: "NOM4D's objective is to enable efficient, scalable construction of very large structures in space," said Andrew Detor, DARPA program manager for NOM4D, in a written statement. "By 'very large,' I mean hundreds of meters or kilometers in scale. Nothing approaching that scale can be achieved today."
paras.zh: DARPA NOM4D 项目经理 Andrew Detor 在一份书面声明中表示：“NOM4D 的目标是在太空中高效、可扩展地建造超大型结构。” “我所说的‘非常大’是指数百米或数百公里的规模。今天还无法达到这个规模。”

paras.en: Such structures could eventually be several football fields long or even extend for kilometers, far beyond the dimensions of conventional spacecraft.
paras.zh: 这种结构最终可能有几个足球场长，甚至延伸数公里，远远超出了传统航天器的尺寸。

paras.en: How Caltech's Construction Robot Reached Space
paras.zh: 加州理工学院的建筑机器人如何到达太空

paras.en: ASTRA began its journey on March 30, 2026, when a SpaceX Transporter-16 mission launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California early that morning.
paras.zh: ASTRA 于 2026 年 3 月 30 日清晨开始了它的旅程，当时 SpaceX Transporter-16 任务从加利福尼亚州范登堡太空部队基地发射升空。

paras.en: The robot traveled aboard Momentus Inc.'s Vigoride 7 orbital vehicle, which carried 10 separate payloads into low Earth orbit. ASTRA occupied approximately one cubic meter of space, a compact package containing both the assembly machinery and the materials required for construction.
paras.zh: 该机器人搭载 Momentus Inc. 的 Vigoride 7 轨道飞行器，该飞行器携带 10 个独立的有效载荷进入近地轨道。 ASTRA 占据了大约一立方米的空间，是一个紧凑的包装，其中包含组装机械和施工所需的材料。

paras.en: Inside were two previously assembled truss bays, reinforced with diagonal tubes and connecting joints. The payload also included a robotic arm and motorized dispensers loaded with the parts needed to construct the remaining sections.
paras.zh: 里面有两个预先组装好的桁架托架，用对角管和连接接头加固。有效载荷还包括机械臂和机动分配器，装载有构建其余部分所需的零件。

paras.en: The successful launch was an emotional moment for the small engineering team watching from Earth. Jaden Suh, a former Caltech postdoctoral scholar who is now an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin, was moved to tears as the spacecraft carrying his team's work headed into orbit.
paras.zh: 对于在地球上观看的小型工程团队来说，成功的发射是一个激动人心的时刻。前加州理工学院博士后学者贾登·苏 (Jaden Suh) 现任德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校助理教授，当载有其团队研究成果的航天器进入轨道时，他感动得热泪盈眶。

paras.en: "As a child, I was super curious about and interested in space structures. Just like many other engineers working in this field, sending your stuff to space is what I've been dreaming of my entire life," Suh says. "I was extremely lucky to have the opportunity to work on this project, beginning from scratch. A lot of my original ideas are included in this system, and it was just incredible seeing it reach space."
paras.zh: “小时候，我对太空结构非常好奇和感兴趣。就像许多其他在这一领域工作的工程师一样，将你的东西送到太空是我一生的梦想，”苏说。 “我非常幸运有机会从头开始参与这个项目。这个系统包含了我的很多原创想法，看到它到达太空真是令人难以置信。”

paras.en: Building a Structure Hundreds of Miles Above Earth
paras.zh: 在距地球数百英里的地方建造一座建筑

paras.en: After ASTRA reached orbit, researchers began operating the system by transmitting instructions to its onboard computer through the Vigoride spacecraft.
paras.zh: ASTRA 到达轨道后，研究人员开始通过 Vigoride 航天器向机载计算机传输指令来操作系统。

paras.en: The initial steps involved releasing the mechanisms that had secured the components during launch. The robot then extended the two previously assembled truss bays out of the machine and proceeded to construct a third bay using the onboard assembly system.
paras.zh: 最初的步骤涉及释放在启动过程中保护组件的机制。然后，机器人将之前组装的两个桁架托架伸出机器，并继续使用机载组装系统构建第三个托架。

paras.en: Three team members managed the construction commands from Earth: Charles Sommer, a former Caltech systems engineer; Alan Truong, a Caltech research engineer; and graduate student Tara Venkatadri (MS '24).
paras.zh: 三名团队成员在地球上负责管理施工命令：查尔斯·索默 (Charles Sommer)，前加州理工学院系统工程师； Alan Truong，加州理工学院研究工程师；和研究生 Tara Venkatadri (MS '24)。

paras.en: Although the robot carried out the assembly operations automatically, the researchers monitored its progress using photographs transmitted from orbit. When something went wrong, they examined the images, adjusted their instructions, and attempted the operation again.
paras.zh: 尽管机器人自动执行组装操作，但研究人员使用从轨道传输的照片监控其进度。当出现问题时，他们检查图像，调整指令，然后再次尝试操作。

paras.en: These setbacks were an important part of learning whether the technology could function outside a controlled laboratory.
paras.zh: 这些挫折是了解该技术是否可以在受控实验室之外发挥作用的重要组成部分。

paras.en: "That's basically the reason you do proof-of-concept testing. There are a lot of differences in the space environment compared to down on Earth," Suh explains. "There are always lots of little surprises."
paras.zh: “这基本上就是进行概念验证测试的原因。与地球上相比，太空环境有很多差异，”Suh 解释道。 “总是有很多小惊喜。”

paras.en: To diagnose problems in orbit, the engineers relied on a second ASTRA system kept at Pellegrino's laboratory at Caltech. This backup unit, known as a flight spare, allowed researchers to recreate difficulties encountered by the spaceborne robot and experiment with possible solutions.
paras.zh: 为了诊断轨道上的问题，工程师们依靠位于加州理工学院佩莱格里诺实验室的第二套 ASTRA 系统。这个被称为飞行备件的备用装置使研究人员能够重现星载机器人遇到的困难并尝试可能的解决方案。

paras.en: "Every time we confirm there is an issue in space, we come to the laboratory and try to mimic the problem on the ground," Sommer says.
paras.zh: “每次我们确认太空中存在问题时，我们都会来到实验室并尝试模仿地面上的问题，”索默说。

paras.en: Communication restrictions made troubleshooting especially challenging. The team could contact ASTRA only during approximately seven or eight brief periods each day, with each opportunity lasting about 15 minutes.
paras.zh: 通信限制使得故障排除变得尤其具有挑战性。该团队每天只能在大约七八个短暂的时间内联系 ASTRA，每次机会持续约 15 分钟。

paras.en: That meant engineers had to make the most of their limited communication windows. They used the laboratory twin to investigate problems, evaluate different solutions, and determine which adjustments were most likely to work. Once a solution was ready, they sent the revised instructions to the robot in orbit.
paras.zh: 这意味着工程师必须充分利用有限的沟通窗口。他们使用实验室双胞胎来调查问题，评估不同的解决方案，并确定哪些调整最有可能起作用。一旦解决方案准备就绪，他们就会将修改后的指令发送给轨道上的机器人。

paras.en: This process helped the team work through numerous unexpected difficulties while gathering valuable information about what future autonomous construction systems will need to operate more reliably.
paras.zh: 这一过程帮助团队克服了许多意想不到的困难，同时收集了有关未来自主施工系统需要什么才能更可靠运行的宝贵信息。

paras.en: ASTRA's intended construction process involves repeating a carefully coordinated series of movements.
paras.zh: ASTRA 的预期施工过程涉及重复一系列精心协调的动作。

paras.en: First, the robotic arm retrieves structural components from their storage dispensers. It positions the tubes and joints on an assembly plate and connects them to create a new truss bay.
paras.zh: 首先，机械臂从存储分配器中检索结构部件。它将管子和接头放置在装配板上，并将它们连接起来以创建新的桁架托架。

paras.en: Once the framework is assembled, the robot is designed to attach a thin reflective film containing many tiny openings. This material forms two reflective cable nets that are held under tension against one another by springs, helping the resulting surface maintain its intended shape.
paras.zh: 一旦框架组装完毕，机器人就会附着一层包含许多微小开口的反射薄膜。这种材料形成两个反射电缆网，通过弹簧相互保持张力，帮助最终的表面保持其预期形状。

paras.en: The special film was jointly invented by researchers at Caltech and the University of Pennsylvania, where the collaborating team was led by Professor Igor Bargatin.
paras.zh: 这种特殊薄膜是由加州理工学院和宾夕法尼亚大学的研究人员联合发明的，合作团队由 Igor Bargatin 教授领导。

paras.en: Unlike the knitted metallic mesh typically used in reflectors designed to fold and unfold, the perforated film requires less tension to maintain its shape. That allows engineers to reduce the amount of supporting structure needed, potentially making the entire assembly substantially lighter.
paras.zh: 与通常用于折叠和展开的反射器中使用的针织金属网不同，穿孔薄膜需要较小的张力来保持其形状。这使得工程师能够减少所需支撑结构的数量，从而有可能使整个组件变得更轻。

paras.en: Lower weight is especially valuable in space engineering because every additional kilogram increases the demands placed on a launch vehicle.
paras.zh: 减轻重量在太空工程中尤其有价值，因为每增加一公斤就会增加对运载火箭的要求。

paras.en: When a bay is finished and its reflective components have been prepared, the robotic system pushes the completed section outward into space. It then begins assembling the next bay.
paras.zh: 当一个隔间完成并准备好其反射部件后，机器人系统会将完成的部分向外推入太空。然后它开始组装下一个海湾。

paras.en: The full ASTRA antenna design calls for 11 connected bays, each attached to the reflective nets and extended outward from the assembly system.
paras.zh: 完整的 ASTRA 天线设计需要 11 个连接的托架，每个托架都连接到反射网上并从装配系统向外延伸。

paras.en: A Small Demonstration With Enormous Implications
paras.zh: 小小的示范却蕴含着巨大的意义

paras.en: Despite successfully demonstrating the construction technique, the researchers do not expect ASTRA to finish assembling all 11 bays before the mission concludes in December.
paras.zh: 尽管成功展示了施工技术，但研究人员预计 ASTRA 不会在 12 月任务结束之前完成所有 11 个隔间的组装。

paras.en: The experiment has revealed several ways the robotic hardware and assembly procedure could be simplified and improved. Even without a completed antenna, the team believes it has collected enough evidence to establish that the approach is technically feasible.
paras.zh: 该实验揭示了简化和改进机器人硬件和组装程序的几种方法。即使没有完整的天线，该团队也相信已经收集了足够的证据来证明该方法在技术上是可行的。

paras.en: The implications extend well beyond the relatively small antenna used in this demonstration.
paras.zh: 其影响远远超出了本演示中使用的相对较小的天线。

paras.en: Future robotic construction systems could help scientists build gigantic space telescopes that collect more light, radio antennas capable of supporting advanced communications, and enormous solar arrays designed to capture sunlight in orbit.
paras.zh: 未来的机器人建筑系统可以帮助科学家建造能够收集更多光线的巨型太空望远镜、能够支持先进通信的无线电天线以及旨在捕获轨道上阳光的巨大太阳能电池阵列。

paras.en: Such solar power systems could potentially transmit collected energy wirelessly to receivers on Earth, an idea being explored through Caltech's Space Solar Power Project.
paras.zh: 这种太阳能系统有可能将收集到的能量无线传输到地球上的接收器，加州理工学院的太空太阳能项目正在探索这一想法。

paras.en: More broadly, the successful test suggests that the size of future space infrastructure may not always have to be dictated by the dimensions of the rockets used to launch its components.
paras.zh: 更广泛地说，成功的测试表明，未来太空基础设施的规模可能并不总是由用于发射其组件的火箭的尺寸决定。

paras.en: "Once you get to the size limit where structures cannot be prebuilt on the ground and unfolded, you have to think about how to build them in space," Pellegrino says. "So, this work could be useful not only for astronomy and astrophysics but also for communications and other areas, such as building very large solar arrays for space solar power."
paras.zh: 佩莱格​​里诺说：“一旦达到无法在地面上预先建造并展开结构的尺寸限制，你就必须考虑如何在太空中建造它们。” “因此，这项工作不仅对天文学和天体物理学有用，而且对通信和其他领域也有用，例如为太空太阳能建造非常大的太阳能电池阵列。”

paras.en: Materials provided by California Institute of Technology. Original written by Kimm Fesenmaier. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州理工学院提供。原创作者：Kimm Fesenmaier。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease

paras.en: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease
paras.zh: 科学家发现橡子与莱姆病之间存在惊人的联系

paras.en: - After more than 35 years of research, scientists have uncovered surprising clues about what really drives Lyme disease risk. Contrary to longstanding assumptions, deer populations appear less important than mice, which can fuel a 40% increase in tick numbers the following year. Even acorn production can predict tick population surges two years in advance, while extreme temperatures may be far less deadly to ticks than scientists once believed.
paras.zh: - 经过超过 35 年的研究，科学家们发现了关于莱姆病风险真正驱动因素的令人惊讶的线索。与长期以来的假设相反，鹿的数量似乎不如老鼠那么重要，而老鼠的数量可能会导致第二年蜱虫数量增加 40%。甚至橡子的生产也可以提前两年预测蜱虫数量的激增，而极端温度对蜱虫的致命性可能远没有科学家曾经认为的那么严重。

paras.en: Tick-borne illnesses are becoming increasingly common across the United States, and Lyme disease remains the most frequently reported. Nearly 500,000 Americans are diagnosed each year. The infection is caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi, which typically reaches humans through the bite of an infected blacklegged tick. Antibiotics can treat Lyme disease, but without treatment, the infection may affect the joints, heart, and nervous system. Some patients also experience symptoms that persist over time.
paras.zh: 蜱传疾病在美国变得越来越常见，而莱姆病仍然是最常报告的疾病。每年有近 50 万美国人被诊断出来。这种感染是由伯氏疏螺旋体细菌引起的，这种细菌通常通过受感染的黑腿蜱叮咬传播到人类。抗生素可以治疗莱姆病，但如果不治疗，感染可能会影响关节、心脏和神经系统。有些患者还会出现持续一段时间的症状。

paras.en: Now, one of the longest-running studies of Lyme disease ecology is challenging several assumptions about what makes the disease more likely to spread. For more than 35 years, scientists at the Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies in Millbrook, New York, have tracked the complicated relationships among ticks, mice, oak trees, predators, and weather. Their research has uncovered unexpected patterns that could help predict when people face greater exposure to infected ticks.
paras.zh: 现在，对莱姆病生态学进行时间最长的研究之一正在挑战关于是什么使该疾病更有可能传播的几个假设。 35 年来，纽约米尔布鲁克卡里生态系统研究所的科学家们一直在追踪蜱虫、老鼠、橡树、捕食者和天气之间的复杂关系。他们的研究发现了意想不到的模式，可以帮助预测人们何时会更多地接触受感染的蜱虫。

paras.en: A new study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences brings together nine of the project's most surprising discoveries. The findings show how decades of observations can reveal connections that shorter studies might miss.
paras.zh: 《美国国家科学院院刊》上发表的一项新研究汇集了该项目的九个最令人惊讶的发现。这些发现表明，数十年的观察如何能够揭示短期研究可能遗漏的联系。

paras.en: "On balance, these surprises have enriched our knowledge of this system, helping us to inform management of tick-borne disease risk," said lead author Richard Ostfeld, a disease ecologist at the Cary Institute who leads the research program alongside Shannon LaDeau.
paras.zh: “总的来说，这些惊喜丰富了我们对这个系统的了解，帮助我们为蜱传疾病风险的管理提供信息，”主要作者理查德·奥斯特菲尔德（Richard Ostfeld）说，他是卡里研究所的疾病生态学家，与香农·拉多（Shannon LaDeau）一起领导了该研究项目。

paras.en: According to Ostfeld, the extensive data collected over the years have been essential for separating meaningful ecological patterns from coincidences and statistical fluctuations.
paras.zh: 奥斯特菲尔德表示，多年来收集的大量数据对于将有意义的生态模式与巧合和统计波动区分开来至关重要。

paras.en: "Studies of this depth and length are incredibly rare," said LaDeau. "This research has followed an ecological community -- including oak trees, mammals, and microorganisms -- examining how interactions like predation, parasitism, and competition shape the system over time. The evolution of understanding summarized in this paper is something you simply cannot get without such a long-term and system-focused study."
paras.zh: “这种深度和长度的研究非常罕见，”拉多说。 “这项研究跟踪了一个生态群落——包括橡树、哺乳​​动物和微生物——研究捕食、寄生和竞争等相互作用如何随着时间的推移塑造系统。如果没有如此长期和以系统为中心的研究，你根本无法获得本文中总结的理解的演变。”

paras.en: Deer May Play a Smaller Role in Lyme Disease Risk Than Expected
paras.zh: 鹿在莱姆病风险中所起的作用可能比预期的要小

paras.en: When Lyme disease first gained recognition in the United States during the 1980s, white-tailed deer were considered a likely driver of rising tick populations. Hunters frequently encountered deer carrying numerous adult ticks, suggesting that areas with more deer might also produce more ticks.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代，当莱姆病首次在美国得到承认时，白尾鹿被认为可能是蜱虫数量增加的推动因素。猎人经常遇到携带大量成年蜱的鹿，这表明鹿较多的地区也可能产生更多的蜱。

paras.en: The reasoning seemed straightforward. Although deer cannot pass the Lyme disease bacterium to ticks, they provide blood meals for adult female ticks. Scientists suspected that larger deer populations would allow more female ticks to reproduce, eventually increasing the number of young ticks capable of spreading the infection.
paras.zh: 推理似乎很简单。虽然鹿不能将莱姆病细菌传递给蜱虫，但它们为成年雌性蜱虫提供血液。科学家怀疑，更多的鹿群会让更多的雌性蜱繁殖，最终增加能够传播感染的幼蜱的数量。

paras.en: But decades of monitoring have produced a different picture. On the Cary Institute's 2,000-acre forested research property in Dutchess County, New York, researchers found no statistically significant connection between deer numbers and the abundance of nymphal ticks. Nymphs are immature ticks responsible for much of the Lyme disease transmission to humans.
paras.zh: 但数十年的监测产生了不同的情况。 On the Cary Institute's 2,000-acre forested research property in Dutchess County, New York, researchers found no statistically significant connection between deer numbers and the abundance of nymphal ticks.若虫是未成熟的蜱虫，负责将莱姆病传播给人类。

paras.en: "We had detected a weak positive relationship between deer and subsequent nymph abundance over short subsets of the data," said Ostfeld, "but the whole data set in its entirety shows no such thing."
paras.zh: 奥斯特菲尔德说：“我们在一小部分数据中发现鹿与随后的若虫丰度之间存在微弱的正相关关系，但整个数据集并没有显示出这样的关系。”

paras.en: Mice Are a Much Stronger Predictor of Tick Surges
paras.zh: 老鼠是蜱虫激增的更强预测者

paras.en: While deer populations failed to predict the abundance of nymphal ticks, mouse populations showed a much clearer relationship.
paras.zh: 虽然鹿群未能预测若虫蜱的丰度，但小鼠群却显示出更清晰的关系。

paras.en: Years with especially large mouse populations were followed by approximately 40% more nymphal ticks the next year. White-footed mice are particularly important because they provide excellent blood meals for tick larvae and are highly effective at transmitting Borrelia burgdorferi to those feeding on them.
paras.zh: 老鼠数量特别多的年份，次年若虫蜱数量会增加约 40%。白足小鼠尤为重要，因为它们为蜱幼虫提供了优质的血粉，并且能够非常有效地将伯氏疏螺旋体传播给以它们为食的蜱虫。

paras.en: Once infected as larvae, ticks can retain the bacteria as they develop into nymphs. When these nymphs take another blood meal, they can pass the infection to humans.
paras.zh: 一旦作为幼虫被感染，蜱虫在发育成若虫时可以保留细菌。当这些若虫再次吸血时，它们可以将感染传染给人类。

paras.en: The findings suggest that tracking mouse populations could provide a valuable early warning of unusually high tick numbers.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，跟踪小鼠种群可以为异常高的蜱数量提供有价值的早期预警。

paras.en: How Acorns Can Predict Tick Populations Two Years Ahead
paras.zh: 橡子如何预测未来两年蜱虫数量

paras.en: One of the most unexpected discoveries involves something that might seem entirely unrelated to Lyme disease: acorns.
paras.zh: 最意想不到的发现之一涉及一些看似与莱姆病完全无关的东西：橡子。

paras.en: Oak trees periodically produce exceptionally large crops of acorns in synchronized events known as acorn masting. These unusually productive years provide an abundance of food for forest rodents, allowing mouse populations to expand during the following year.
paras.zh: 橡树会定期产生大量的橡子，这种同步事件被称为“橡子肥大”。这些异常多产的年份为森林啮齿动物提供了丰富的食物，使老鼠的数量在接下来的一年中得以扩大。

paras.en: That increase in mice then supports larger numbers of young ticks. As a result, the researchers found that a particularly heavy acorn crop can reliably predict an increase in nymphal ticks two years later.
paras.zh: 老鼠数量的增加支持了更多数量的幼蜱。结果，研究人员发现，特别重的橡子作物可以可靠地预测两年后若虫蜱的增加。

paras.en: The relationship reveals a remarkable sequence of events in which the reproductive cycle of forest trees helps determine future tick abundance. It also offers researchers another potential tool for anticipating periods of greater Lyme disease exposure.
paras.zh: 这种关系揭示了一系列显着的事件序列，其中林木的繁殖周期有助于确定未来蜱虫的丰度。它还为研究人员提供了另一种潜在的工具来预测莱姆病的高暴露期。
